start.name: Sonker Bulk Liquids Terminal, Basin 3, Sokhna Port, Ain Sokhna, Egypt
start.coord_basis: Wikipedia coordinate for Ain Sokhna port/town (29°36'00"N 32°19'00"E) — general port-area location only; Sonker's Basin 3 terminal sits within Ain Sokhna/Sokhna Port but no more precise public coordinate was found for the jetty itself

prior_research.notes: Sonker (Sonker Bunkering Company / Sonker Energy) operates the Bulk Liquids Terminal at Sokhna Port, Ain Sokhna, Gulf of Suez — a site that berths FSRUs and feeds regasified LNG into Egypt's national gas grid via dedicated pipelines built 'outside the port fence' (IFC ESRS disclosure, re: an adjacent line as an analogue). Two FSRUs began operating from Sonker in 2015 -- Hoegh Gallant (March, 500 MMSCFD) and BW Singapore (November, 750 MMSCFD) (Sonker company history page) -- a plausible basis for GEM's 'Phase 1'/'Phase 2' gas-line split (one grid tie-in per FSRU), but no source names which phase is 9 km vs 7 km, nor identifies the specific national-grid valve/metering station each ties into. A separate, later (2025) GASCO/Petrojet gas-import pipeline (17 km, 36-inch, 3 valve rooms, built by Petrojet) for a third FSRU at Sonker is documented in the two Daily News Egypt articles -- that is a newer, distinct project, not P8006/P8007. Could not source a specific end-point name/coordinate for either phase this session (WebSearch budget exhausted mid-task, shared across concurrent research). Recommend a follow-up pass targeting GASCO's network map / EIA filings to pin the tie-in point, and to determine which phase is 9 km vs 7 km.

end.name: Ras Bakr Transmission Station
end.coord_basis: GeoNames gazetteer entry 'Ra's Bakr' (point feature, N28 23'31" E33 3'42"), Red Sea Governorate, Egypt -- the nearest named public gazetteer entry to the transmission station named in the trade-press source below; GeoNames also separately lists a 'Ra's Bakr' oilfield ~14 km further NW (N28 29'0" E32 57'0"), confirming this as a real, long-standing place name in the Ras Gharib oil/gas cluster, not a typo

prior_research.sheet_conflicts: Sheet StartLocation 'Petreco Plant' is confirmed as an accurate, verbatim name (not a misspelling) -- it appears exactly as 'Petreco Plant' in the source table below. EndLocation is currently blank on the sheet and should be 'Ras Bakr Transmission Station'.
prior_research.notes: Egypt Oil & Gas Newspaper's Sept 2020 report 'Gulf of Suez, Eastern Desert and Sinai: Egypt's Crude Oil Squad' (PDF) contains a table 'Natural Gas Infrastructure in the Gulf of Suez/Sinai' listing seven pipelines; one row reads exactly: 'Trans Gulf Gas | Petreco Plant | Ras Bakr Transmission Station | 75 km | 12 in | 110 mmcf/d' -- an exact match to the sheet's 75.0 km length and StartLocation text. Body text independently confirms: 'Two of the seven pipelines (i.e. Trans Gulf Gas and Zaafarana-Korimat pipelines) transport natural gas to be pumped in two stations: Ras Bakr Transmission Station and Korimat Power Station.' NOTE ON VERIFICATION: url_verifier.py FAILs this URL on the 'Trans Gulf' substring check because the source is an embedded-text PDF whose two-column table layout the extractor doesn't parse cleanly -- this is the documented PDF-extraction false-negative case, not evidence the page is dead/wrong. I downloaded the PDF via WebFetch and ran `pdftotext -layout` and `pdftotext` (no layout) locally myself; both cleanly show 'Petreco Plant' / 'Ras Bakr' / 'Transmission Station' as contiguous text, confirming the table content directly rather than relying on the substring screen. Could not independently geocode 'Petreco Plant' itself -- no gazetteer, company database, or press mention of a facility by that name was found in GeoNames or the sources reachable this session (WebSearch tool quota was exhausted session-wide before this could be searched further; site/company-name searches via direct WebFetch on Google/Bing/DuckDuckGo all failed on bot-detection). Recommend a follow-up pass with fresh search budget for 'Petreco' as a company/plant name in the Ras Gharib gas-processing cluster (candidates worth checking: GPC, Petrobel/Belayim, Petrozeit, Petrogulf -- several similarly-named JVs operate gas processing in this exact area per Suez Oil Company's own facilities page). Until then this PID should stay resolved:false since only one endpoint has a real coordinate.
